title: Provider-neutral publication and CI implementation bridge

observations.head_rule: branch.head, commit.id, review.target_head, merge_handoff.target_head, ci.target_head, and publication.target_head are identical
observations.signature_rule: commit.signature.status is valid and commit.dco.status is signed; these are supplied observations, not cryptographic verification
observations.handoff_rule: review is approved and merge_handoff is ready; no merge or publication is performed
observations.ci_rule: CI success is correlated to the review and exact head but remains verification: unverified
observations.evidence_rule: Each component and the review/CI/head correlation has exactly one unique canonical SHA-256 evidence reference

privacy.allowed_values: bounded identifiers, enumerations, booleans, and SHA-256 or Git object digests

failure_semantics.side_effects: The model and checker perform no network, provider, Git, CI, review-system, merge, publication, or durable-state operation.

limitations: A valid envelope proves only that supplied observations are structurally and digest-consistent.
The checker does not inspect Git or CI, verify cryptography or DCO trailers, contact a review system, merge, publish, or establish remote or hosted-CI success.
Review, merge handoff, and CI statuses are observations for Coordinator and AWQ policy, not runtime approvals or task transitions.
follow_up: Coordinator remains authoritative for task identity, revisions, claims, leases, and durable state.
AWQ remains authoritative for requirements, gates, and evidence acceptance.
A future integration may consume this envelope only through approved Coordinator and AWQ contracts.
